summary: Tested ZIP-based article import at /admin/blog/import. UI flow works perfectly (upload, parse, mapping, validation). Import step FAILS — backend /api/admin/upload rejects the first image with 'Invalid file type. Allowed: image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, image/webp'. Root cause: JSZip's entry.async('blob') returns a Blob without a MIME type, so the multipart upload sends Content-Type 'application/octet-stream', which the backend rejects even though the extension .webp is allowed. 0 posts created; steps 8-10 (post + featured_image + files verification) could not be validated.

critical.issue: Rejects ZIP-imported images (MIME inference via Content-Type). Blobs extracted by JSZip have no type → Content-Type defaults to application/octet-stream. Upload returns 400 'Invalid file type. Allowed: image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, image/webp' even though extension is .webp. Entire ZIP import flow is blocked.

integration_issues.issue: uploadOneImage() in /app/frontend/app/admin/blog/import/page.tsx passes the raw Blob from JSZip without setting a MIME type. Fix: when constructing the FormData, wrap the blob with an explicit type inferred from the filename extension, e.g. `new File([blob], fileName, { type: mimeFromExt(fileName) })` or `new Blob([await blob.arrayBuffer()], { type: 'image/webp' })`. Alternatively backend should trust extension when content_type is octet-stream.

issues: Cookie consent banner overlays the login submit button (z-[9998] fixed div) — blocks clicks until user accepts/dismisses. Consider suppressing the banner on /admin routes or lowering its z-index below the form.

action_items: FIX (frontend): In /app/frontend/app/admin/blog/import/page.tsx `uploadOneImage`, infer MIME type from filename extension (.webp→image/webp, .jpg/.jpeg→image/jpeg, .png→image/png, .gif→image/gif) and construct `new File([blob], fileName, { type: mime })` before appending to FormData. This is the minimal, targeted fix — frontend owns the ZIP extraction.
ALTERNATIVE FIX (backend): Relax /api/admin/upload MIME check to accept application/octet-stream when the filename extension matches the allowed list.
FIX (UX): Dismiss or z-index-lower the cookie consent banner on /admin pages so login is clickable without first accepting cookies.
RETEST: After fix, re-run this exact flow; all 10 steps should pass, including backend verification of featured_image, is_published=false, hygiene_section auto-insertion, and social_only exclusion.

rca of the issue: Root cause: In /app/frontend/app/admin/blog/import/page.tsx the helper `uploadOneImage(blob, fileName)` appends the raw Blob that JSZip returns via `entry.async('blob')`. JSZip does not set a MIME type on these blobs, so when the browser serializes the multipart/form-data request the file part Content-Type becomes 'application/octet-stream'. FastAPI's UploadFile.content_type reflects this. The backend /api/admin/upload validator (in /app/backend/routers/blog.py per review context) checks content_type against ['image/jpeg','image/png','image/gif','image/webp'] and returns 400 'Invalid file type…'. The misleading part of the error is that it lists image/webp as allowed — the filename IS .webp but its MIME isn't. Reproduction: upload /tmp/zip_test/article-import.zip → mapping shows 4 assets 'намерен' → click import → first image upload returns 400 → frontend shows '❌ Грешка при импорт: karvyashti-ventsi-pri-miene-hero.webp: Invalid file type…'. Mitigation (preferred, 2-line frontend patch): map extension→MIME and rebuild file as `new File([blob], fileName, { type: mime })` before FormData.append. Alternative backend patch: accept octet-stream when filename extension ∈ allowed list.
